17.8 A whole-space bound for the good auxiliary labels
The logarithmic dimension comparison under restriction, together with the actual occurring-label
dimension bound on the bad copies, yields an operator inequality before measuring a physical
excitation component.

17.9 The good auxiliary observable on a whole label
The preceding whole-space comparison restricts to each actual whole-copy label subspace. The
restricted good-copy observable retains the whole logarithmic dimension, up to the same bad-
copy and binomial corrections.

Proof. ✓ Proof Every permutation of the good copies is also a whole-copy permutation, so it
commutes with the whole-copy central projection. Summing the central projections of the good-
copy representation proves the stated commutation. Compress the preceding whole-space upper
bound for 𝐹𝑤 by 𝑃𝜆. Since 𝑃𝜆 is an orthogonal projection and 𝐹𝑤𝑃𝜆 = (log 𝑑𝜆)𝑃𝜆, the compressed
inequality is exactly the stated lower bound. This argument also includes 𝑃𝜆 = 0.
This is the whole-label support step in [ Ope26b, Section 7, equation (comparator:good-
auxiliary)]. To apply it to an actual physical excitation component, the whole-copy auxiliary
label must be preserved under that physical projection.
17.10 The good auxiliary label on an excitation component
A physical excitation measurement acts on a different tensor factor from an auxiliary whole-
label projection. The selected component consequently retains that label, and the compressed
good-copy bound applies to it.

label-support contribution to [ Ope26b, Section 7, equation (comparator:good-auxiliary)]. The
numerical whole-label threshold and metric comparison are separate steps, and no commutation
